- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing the true mean-reversion path.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, particularly when true values show a downward trend.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward moves in history; model reacts too aggressively, then corrects too quickly.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values when recent history shows strong downward momentum.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward if the last 5–7 days show a clear downward trend.
- Model tends to ignore long-term mean reversion; should apply a smoothing factor to reduce overreaction to short-term volatility.
- When true values drop below 70, model should reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overestimating recovery.
